units.en: Under the Zhou, the old Xia office became the office of Sima, the marshal.
units.literal: Under the Zhou, the Xia ministry was styled Marshal (Sima).

units.zh: 其後程伯休父，周宣王時，以世官克平徐方，錫以官族，因而為氏。
units.en: Later, Cheng Bo Xiufu—during King Xuan of Zhou—used his hereditary charge to crush the Xu region and received a clan designation from his title; from that the Sima surname arose.
units.literal: Later Cheng Bo Xiufu, in the reign of King Xuan of Zhou, by virtue of his hereditary office conquered and pacified the Xu lands and was granted a clan name taken from his office; his descendants therefore took Sima as their surname.

units.zh: 楚漢間，司馬卬為趙將，與諸侯伐秦。
units.en: In the turmoil between Chu and Han, Sima Ang commanded troops for Zhao and marched with the alliance against Qin.
units.literal: Between Chu and Han, Sima Ang served as a Zhao general and joined the feudal lords in attacking Qin.

units.zh: 秦亡，立為殷王，都河內。
units.en: After Qin collapsed he was enthroned as king of Yin with his seat at Henei.
units.literal: When Qin fell, [Ang] was established as King of Yin and made his capital in Henei.

units.zh: 漢以其地為郡，子孫遂家焉。
units.en: The Han turned that territory into a commandery, and his line took root there.
units.literal: Han converted his territory into a commandery, and his descendants settled there.

units.zh: 自卬八世，生征西將軍鈞，字叔平。
units.en: Eight generations down from Ang came General Who Guards the West Jun, whose courtesy name was Shuping.
units.literal: Eight generations after Ang was born General Who Guards the West Jun, courtesy name Shuping.

units.zh: 鈞生豫章太守量，字公度。
units.en: Jun’s son was Liang, prefect of Yuzhang, courtesy name Gongdu.
units.literal: Jun fathered Prefect of Yuzhang Liang, courtesy name Gongdu.

units.zh: 量生潁川太守儁，字元異。
units.en: Liang’s son was Jun, prefect of Yingchuan, courtesy name Yuanyi.
units.literal: Liang fathered Prefect of Yingchuan Jun, courtesy name Yuanyi.

units.zh: 儁生京兆尹防，字建公。
units.en: Jun’s son was Fang, governor of Jingzhao, courtesy name Jiangong.
units.literal: Jun fathered Governor of the Metropolitan Region Fang, courtesy name Jiangong.

units.zh: 帝即防之第二子也。
units.en: He was the second son of Fang.
units.literal: The Emperor was Fang’s second son.

units.zh: 少有奇節，聰朗多大略，博學洽聞，伏膺儒教。
units.en: Even young he revealed unusual steadfastness—acute, far-sighted, erudite, and steeped in the Confucian canon.
units.literal: In youth he showed uncommon integrity; he was bright and broad in strategic grasp, widely read and well informed, and devoted himself to Confucian teaching.

units.zh: 漢末大亂，常慨然有憂天下心。
units.en: As Han unraveled, he was repeatedly consumed by anxiety for the empire.
units.literal: At the end of Han, when great turmoil arose, he often felt stirred with concern for the realm.

units.zh: 南陽太守同郡楊俊名知人，[1]見帝，未弱冠，以為非常之器。
units.en: Yang Jun of Nanyang—his fellow townsman and a celebrated judge of talent—met him before his cap-and-girdle ceremony and pronounced him a figure of rare promise.
units.literal: Yang Jun of the same commandery, prefect of Nanyang, famed for judging men,[1] met the Emperor before his twentieth year and deemed him an extraordinary vessel.

units.zh: 尚書清河崔琰與帝兄朗善，亦謂朗曰：「君弟聰亮明允，剛斷英特，非子所及也。」
units.en: Cui Yan of Qinghe, who served in the Secretariat, was close to his elder brother Sima Lang and told Lang, “Your brother combines lucidity with integrity and carries an iron decisiveness—you cannot rival him.”
units.literal: Minister Cui Yan of Qinghe was on good terms with the Emperor’s elder brother Lang and also said to Lang, “Your younger brother is clear-sighted and fair-minded, resolute and extraordinary—not someone you can match.”

units.zh: 漢建安六年，郡舉上計掾。
units.en: In Han’s sixth Jian’an year the commandery recommended him as clerk for the capital assessment.
units.literal: In the sixth year of Jian’an of Han, the commandery nominated him as clerk for the annual accounts.

units.zh: 魏武帝為司空，聞而辟之。
units.en: Cao Cao, then minister of works, heard of him and summoned him to service.
units.literal: Emperor Wu of Wei was Minister of Works and, hearing of him, summoned him.

units.zh: 帝知漢運方微，不欲屈節曹氏，辭以風痹，不能起居。
units.en: Knowing the Han house was in decline, he refused to bend himself to the Cao clan and pleaded crippling wind paralysis that kept him from rising.
units.literal: The Emperor knew Han’s mandate was failing and did not wish to bend his integrity to the Cao house; he declined on the grounds of wind paralysis and inability to rise.

units.zh: 魏武使人夜往密刺之，帝堅臥不動。
units.en: Cao Cao sent someone at night to stab him secretly, but Sima Yi lay rigidly in bed and did not move.
units.literal: Emperor Wu sent someone by night to stab him secretly; the Emperor lay rigid and did not move.

units.zh: 及魏武為丞相，又辟為文學掾，敕行者曰：「若復盤桓，便收之。」
units.en: When Cao Cao became Chancellor he summoned him again as literary clerk and told the courier, “If he hesitates once more, seize him.”
units.literal: When Emperor Wu became Chancellor, he again summoned him as clerk for literature and instructed the messenger: “If he stalls again, arrest him.”

units.zh: 帝懼而就職。
units.en: Terrified, he accepted the appointment.
units.literal: The Emperor, in fear, took the post.

units.zh: 於是使與太子游處，遷黃門侍郎，轉議郎、丞相東曹屬，尋轉主簿。
units.en: Thereafter he was assigned to attend the crown prince, promoted to Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates, transferred to Consultant and then aide in the Chancellor's Eastern Bureau, and soon made chief clerk.
units.literal: Thereafter he was assigned to attend the crown prince, promoted to Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates, transferred to Consultant and then aide in the Chancellor's Eastern Bureau, and soon made chief clerk.

units.zh: 從討張魯，言於魏武曰：「劉備以詐力虜劉璋，蜀人未附而遠爭江陵，此機不可失也。
units.en: On the expedition against Zhang Lu he urged Cao Cao: “Liu Bei bullied his way into Yi through trickery; the Shu populace still mistrusts him while he reaches for Jiangling—do not let this opening slip.
units.literal: Accompanying the campaign against Zhang Lu, he said to Emperor Wu, “Liu Bei seized Liu Zhang by deceit and force; the people of Shu are not yet attached, yet he contests Jiangling from afar—this opportunity must not be missed.

units.zh: 今若曜威漢中，益州震動，進兵臨之，勢必瓦解。
units.en: Show strength in Hanzhong and Yi province will reel; press forward and their front will collapse.
units.literal: If we now display our might in Hanzhong, Yizhou will be shaken; advance the army against it and it will surely crumble.

units.zh: 因此之勢，易為功力。
units.en: Ride that tide and the task becomes straightforward.
units.literal: Riding this momentum, success will come easily.

units.zh: 聖人不能違時，亦不失時矣。」
units.en: Even the sage neither fights the moment nor lets it pass unused.”
units.literal: The sage cannot defy the hour, yet neither does he miss it.”

units.zh: 魏武曰：「人苦無足，既得隴右，復欲得蜀！」
units.en: Cao Cao replied, “People are never satisfied—take Longyou and they hunger for Shu!”
units.literal: Emperor Wu said, “Men suffer from insatiable greed—having gained Longyou, they want Shu too!”

units.zh: 言竟不從。
units.en: He would not take the counsel.
units.literal: In the end he did not follow the advice.

units.zh: 既而從討孫權，破之。
units.en: He later joined the campaign against Sun Quan and helped rout him.
units.literal: He then accompanied the campaign against Sun Quan and defeated him.

units.zh: 軍還，權遣使乞降，上表稱臣，陳說天命。
units.en: On the army’s return Sun Quan sent envoys suing for peace, presented a memorial as a vassal, and rehearsed Heaven’s mandate.
units.literal: When the army returned, Sun Quan sent envoys begging to surrender, submitted a memorial declaring himself a subject, and expounded the mandate of Heaven.

units.zh: 魏武帝曰：「此兒欲踞吾著爐炭上邪！」
units.en: Cao Cao snapped, “Does that boy mean to roast me over live coals?”
units.literal: Emperor Wu of Wei said, “Does this fellow want to seat me on coals over a furnace?”

units.zh: 答曰：「漢運垂終，殿下十分天下而有其九，以服事之。
units.en: He answered: “The Han flame gutters while you hold nine parts in ten yet still bow to the emperor.
units.literal: He replied: “Han’s mandate is near its end; Your Highness holds nine-tenths of the realm yet still serves it.

units.zh: 權之稱臣，天人之意也。
units.en: Sun Quan’s offer to submit answers both Heaven and the human heart.
units.literal: Sun Quan’s submission accords with the will of Heaven and men.

units.zh: 虞、夏、殷、周不以謙讓者，畏天知命也。」
units.en: The sage-kings of Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou yielded not from timidity but because they revered Heaven and accepted its mandate.”
units.literal: Yu, Xia, Yin, and Zhou did not yield out of mere modesty—they feared Heaven and knew the mandate.”

units.zh: 魏國既建，遷太子中庶子。
units.en: Once the Wei kingdom was founded he rose to palace attendant to the heir apparent.
units.literal: When the state of Wei was established, he was promoted to palace attendant to the heir apparent.

units.zh: 每與大謀，輒有奇策，為太子所信重，與陳羣、吳質、朱鑠號曰四友。
units.en: In every grand council he supplied sharp schemes; the heir relied on him and paired him with Chen Qun, Wu Zhi, and Zhu Shuo as the “Four Friends.”
units.literal: Whenever major plans were laid he produced striking stratagems; the heir trusted and esteemed him, and with Chen Qun, Wu Zhi, and Zhu Shuo he was called the Four Friends.

units.zh: 遷為軍司馬，言於魏武曰：「昔箕子陳謀，以食為首。
units.en: Promoted army marshal, he told Cao Cao: “When Jizi advised the king, grain came first.
units.literal: He was promoted to army marshal and said to Emperor Wu, “When Jizi presented his counsel, he put food first.

units.zh: 今天下不耕者蓋二十餘萬，非經國遠籌也。
units.en: Today more than two hundred thousand people are not farming; that is no long-range plan for governing the state.
units.literal: Today perhaps two hundred thousand men do not till the soil—this is no far-reaching policy for governing the state.

units.zh: 雖戎甲未卷，自宜且耕且守。」
units.en: Even while armor has not yet been put away, we should farm and defend at the same time.”
units.literal: Though armor is not yet laid aside, we should farm and defend at the same time.”

units.zh: 魏武納之，於是務農積穀，國用豐贍。
units.en: Cao Cao agreed; farming and granaries were stressed until state stores overflowed.
units.literal: Emperor Wu accepted this; agriculture was emphasized and grain stored, and state supplies grew ample.

units.zh: 帝又言荊州刺史胡脩粗暴，南鄉太守傅方驕奢，並不可居邊。
units.en: He further warned that Hu Xiu, inspector of Jingzhou, was brutish and Fu Fang, prefect of Nanxiang, was decadent—neither belonged on the border.
units.literal: The Emperor also said that Hu Xiu, inspector of Jingzhou, was brutal and coarse, and Fu Fang, prefect of Nanxiang, arrogant and extravagant—neither was fit to hold the frontier.

units.zh: 魏武不之察。
units.en: Cao Cao brushed the warning aside.
units.literal: Emperor Wu did not heed him.

units.zh: 及蜀將關羽圍曹仁於樊，于禁等七軍皆沒，脩、方果降羽，而仁圍甚急焉。
units.en: When Guan Yu of Shu penned Cao Ren at Fan and Yu Jin’s seven corps vanished beneath the flood, Hu Xiu and Fu Fang duly defected to Guan Yu and the siege of Fan tightened unbearably.
units.literal: When Shu general Guan Yu besieged Cao Ren at Fan and Yu Jin’s seven armies were drowned, Hu and Fu indeed surrendered to Guan Yu, and Ren’s siege grew desperate.

units.zh: 是時漢帝都許昌，魏武以為近賊，欲徙河北。
units.en: The Han emperor still sat at Xuchang; Cao Cao judged it perilously near the foe and planned to shift the court north of the river.
units.literal: At that time the Han emperor was at Xuchang; Emperor Wu thought it too close to the enemy and wished to move the capital north of the Yellow River.

units.zh: 帝諫曰：「禁等為水所沒，非戰守之所失，於國家大計未有所損，而便遷都，既示敵以弱，又淮沔之人大不安矣。
units.en: He objected: “Yu Jin’s men drowned—they were not routed in the field. The empire’s strategy is intact; relocating now advertises fear and panics everyone between the Huai and the Han.
units.literal: The Emperor remonstrated: “Yu Jin and the others were lost to water, not to defeat in battle or defense—the state’s grand plan is not yet harmed. To move the capital rashly would show weakness to the enemy and greatly unsettle the people between the Huai and the Han.

units.zh: 孫權、劉備，外親內疏，羽之得意，權所不願也。
units.en: Sun Quan and Liu Bei are allies in name alone; Sun Quan cannot relish Guan Yu’s triumph.
units.literal: Sun Quan and Liu Bei are outward kin but inwardly estranged; Guan Yu’s triumph is not what Quan desires.

units.zh: 可喻權所，令掎其後，則樊圍自解。」
units.en: Urge Sun Quan to stab Guan Yu in the rear and the ring around Fan loosens on its own.”
units.literal: You may instruct Quan to strike Guan Yu from behind; then the siege of Fan will lift of itself.”

units.zh: 魏武從之。
units.en: Cao Cao adopted the plan.
units.literal: Emperor Wu followed this advice.

units.zh: 權果遣將呂蒙西襲公安，拔之，羽遂為蒙所獲。
units.en: Sun Quan dispatched Lü Meng westward against Gong’an, seized it, and Guan Yu fell into Meng’s hands.
units.literal: Quan indeed sent general Lü Meng to raid Gong’an from the west and took it; Guan Yu was then captured by Meng.

units.zh: 魏武以荊州遺黎及屯田在潁川者逼近南寇，[2]皆欲徙之。
units.en: Cao Cao meant to uproot the leftover households of Jingzhou and the military colonies in Yingchuan because both fronts skirted the southern enemy.
units.literal: Emperor Wu wished to relocate the remnant people of Jingzhou and the agricultural colonies in Yingchuan because they lay close to the southern foe.

units.zh: 帝曰：「荊楚輕脫，易動難安。
units.en: He replied, “The Jing-Chu folk are restless—quick to bolt and slow to reassure.
units.literal: The Emperor said, “The people of Jing-Chu are flighty—easy to stir, hard to settle.

units.zh: 關羽新破，諸為惡者藏竄觀望。
units.en: Guan Yu’s fall leaves malcontents skulking in the shadows, watching.
units.literal: Guan Yu has just been defeated; those who meant harm hide and watch.

units.zh: 今徙其善者，既傷其意，將令去者不敢復還。」
units.en: Uproot the loyal now and you crush their hearts; refugees will never dare come home.”
units.literal: If we now relocate the good among them, we wound their feelings and will make those who flee dare not return.”

units.zh: 從之。
units.en: Cao Cao relented.
units.literal: [Emperor Wu] followed this.

units.zh: 其後諸亡者悉復業。
units.en: Later every exile drifted back to his fields.
units.literal: Afterwards all who had fled resumed their occupations.

units.zh: 及魏武薨于洛陽，朝野危懼。
units.en: When Cao Cao died at Luoyang, court and capital trembled.
units.literal: When Emperor Wu died at Luoyang, court and countryside were fearful.

units.zh: 帝綱紀喪事，內外肅然。
units.en: He imposed discipline on the mourning rites until palace and province stood calm.
units.literal: The Emperor directed the funeral rites; within and without there was solemn order.

units.zh: 乃奉梓宮還鄴。
units.en: He convoyed the royal catafalque back to Ye.
units.literal: He then escorted the coffin back to Ye.

units.zh: 魏文帝即位，封河津亭侯，轉丞相長史。
units.en: When Emperor Wen of Wei ascended the throne, Sima Yi was enfeoffed as Marquis of Hejin Village and transferred to be chief clerk to the chancellor.
units.literal: When Emperor Wen of Wei ascended the throne, Sima Yi was enfeoffed as Marquis of Hejin Village and transferred to be chief clerk to the chancellor.

units.zh: 會孫權帥兵西過，朝議以樊、襄陽無穀，不可以禦寇。
units.en: At the time, Sun Quan led troops westward. Court discussion held that Fan and Xiangyang had no grain and could not be used to resist the invaders.
units.literal: At the time, Sun Quan led troops westward. Court discussion held that Fan and Xiangyang had no grain and could not be used to resist the invaders.

units.zh: 時曹仁鎮襄陽，請召仁還宛。
units.en: At the time Cao Ren was stationed at Xiangyang, and they requested that Ren be summoned back to Wan.
units.literal: At the time Cao Ren was stationed at Xiangyang, and they requested that Ren be summoned back to Wan.

units.zh: 帝曰：「孫權新破關羽，此其欲自結之時也，必不敢為患。襄陽水陸之衝，禦寇要害，不可棄也。」
units.en: The emperor said, "Sun Quan has only just defeated Guan Yu; this is the moment when he wants to secure his own position, and he certainly will not dare become a menace. Xiangyang is a crossing point for water and land routes and a vital place for resisting invaders; it cannot be abandoned."
units.literal: The emperor said, "Sun Quan has only just defeated Guan Yu; this is the moment when he wants to secure his own position, and he certainly will not dare become a menace. Xiangyang is a crossing point for water and land routes and a vital place for resisting invaders; it cannot be abandoned."

units.zh: 言竟不從。
units.en: In the end, his words were not followed.
units.literal: In the end, his words were not followed.

units.zh: 仁遂焚棄二城，權果不為寇，魏文悔之。
units.en: Ren accordingly burned and abandoned the two cities. Quan indeed did not invade, and Emperor Wen of Wei regretted it.
units.literal: Ren accordingly burned and abandoned the two cities. Quan indeed did not invade, and Emperor Wen of Wei regretted it.

units.zh: 及魏受漢禪，以帝為尚書。
units.en: When Wei received Han's abdication, the emperor was made minister in the Secretariat.
units.literal: When Wei received Han's abdication, the emperor was made minister in the Secretariat.

units.zh: 頃之，轉督軍、御史中丞，封安國鄉侯。
units.en: Before long, he was transferred to be army supervisor and palace aide to the censor-in-chief, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Anguo Township.
units.literal: Before long, he was transferred to be army supervisor and palace aide to the censor-in-chief, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Anguo Township.

units.zh: 黃初二年，督軍官罷，遷侍中、尚書右僕射。
units.en: In Huangchu’s second year the army-supervisor post was scrapped; he became palace attendant and right vice director of the Secretariat.
units.literal: In the second year of Huangchu (221), the office of supervisor of armies was abolished; he was promoted to palace attendant and right vice director of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 五年，天子南巡，觀兵吳疆。
units.en: In the fifth year the emperor toured south and drilled troops along Wu’s frontier.
units.literal: In the fifth year (224), the Son of Heaven toured south and reviewed troops on Wu’s border.

units.zh: 帝留鎮許昌，改封向鄉侯，轉撫軍、假節，領兵五千，加給事中、錄尚書事。
units.en: He stayed to hold Xuchang, was re-enfeoffed as marquis of Xiang township, promoted Protector of the Army with credential axe, led five thousand soldiers, and added duties as palace attendant and overseer of Secretariat business.
units.literal: The Emperor remained to guard Xuchang, was enfeoffed as marquis of Xiang township, became Protector of the Army with ceremonial axe, commanded five thousand troops, and was given concurrent posts as attendant within the palace and recorder of Secretariat affairs.

units.zh: 帝固辭。
units.en: He firmly declined.
units.literal: The Emperor firmly declined.

units.zh: 天子曰：「吾於庶事，以夜繼晝，無須臾寧息。
units.en: The emperor said, “I chase paperwork from dusk to dawn without a breath’s pause.
units.literal: The Son of Heaven said, “In routine affairs I follow night with day without a moment’s rest.

units.zh: 此非以為榮，乃分憂耳。」
units.en: That burden is not glory—it is sharing the weight on my shoulders.”
units.literal: This is not for honor—it is to share my burdens.”

units.zh: 六年，天子復大興舟師征吳，復命帝居守，內鎮百姓，外供軍資。
units.en: The sixth year brought another massive river expedition against Wu; again he was told to stay behind—steady the interior and provision the campaign.
units.literal: In the sixth year (225), the Son of Heaven again raised a great fleet to campaign against Wu and again ordered the Emperor to remain as guardian—pacifying the people within and supplying the army without.

units.zh: 臨行，詔曰：「吾深以後事為念，故以委卿。
units.en: Before embarking he proclaimed: “I brood over what follows my reign—so I lay it in your hands.
units.literal: On departure he issued an edict: “I think deeply on what comes after me; therefore I entrust you.

units.zh: 曹參雖有戰功，而蕭何為重。
units.en: Cao Shen won battles, yet Xiao He anchored the state.
units.literal: Cao Shen had battle merit, yet Xiao He mattered more.

units.zh: 使吾無西顧之憂，不亦可乎！」
units.en: Free my mind from the western march—is that too much to ask!”
units.literal: Let me have no worry over the west—is that not enough!”

units.zh: 天子自廣陵還洛陽，詔帝曰：「吾東，撫軍當總西事；
units.en: Returning from Guangling to Luoyang he decreed: “When I march east, the Protector commands the west;
units.literal: When the Son of Heaven returned from Guangling to Luoyang, he issued an edict to the Emperor: “When I am east, the Protector of the Army shall oversee the west;

units.zh: 吾西，撫軍當總東事。」
units.en: when I march west, the Protector commands the east.”
units.literal: when I am west, the Protector of the Army shall oversee the east.”

units.zh: 於是帝留鎮許昌。
units.en: So he continued to anchor Xuchang.
units.literal: Thereupon the Emperor remained to guard Xuchang.

units.zh: 及天子疾篤，帝與曹真、陳羣等見於崇華殿之南堂，並受顧命輔政。
units.en: When the Son of Heaven became gravely ill, the emperor, Cao Zhen, Chen Qun, and others met him in the south hall of Chonghua Palace and together received his final charge to assist in government.
units.literal: When the Son of Heaven became gravely ill, the emperor, Cao Zhen, Chen Qun, and others met him in the south hall of Chonghua Palace and together received his final charge to assist in government.

units.zh: 詔太子曰：「有間此三公者，慎勿疑之。」
units.en: He instructed the crown prince, saying, "If anyone sows discord against these three lords, be careful not to doubt them."
units.literal: He instructed the crown prince, saying, "If anyone sows discord against these three lords, be careful not to doubt them."

units.zh: 明帝即位，改封舞陽侯。
units.en: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, Sima Yi's enfeoffment was changed to Marquis of Wuyang.
units.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, Sima Yi's enfeoffment was changed to Marquis of Wuyang.

units.zh: 及孫權圍江夏，遣其將諸葛瑾、張霸并攻襄陽，帝督諸軍討權，走之。
units.en: When Sun Quan invested Jiangxia and Zhuge Jin with Zhang Ba struck Xiangyang together, he led the host against Sun Quan and threw him back.
units.literal: When Sun Quan besieged Jiangxia and sent his generals Zhuge Jin and Zhang Ba jointly to attack Xiangyang, the Emperor commanded the armies against Quan and drove him off.

units.zh: 進擊，敗瑾，斬霸，并首級千餘。
units.en: He pressed the pursuit, routed Zhuge Jin, slew Zhang Ba, and piled up more than a thousand heads.
units.literal: Pressing the attack, he defeated Jin, beheaded Ba, and took over a thousand heads.

units.zh: 遷驃騎將軍。
units.en: He was elevated to general of the agile cavalry.
units.literal: He was promoted to general of agile cavalry.

units.zh: 太和元年六月，天子詔帝屯于宛，加督荊、豫二州諸軍事。
units.en: In the sixth month of the first year of Taihe (227), the Son of Heaven ordered the emperor to garrison at Wan and additionally placed him in command of military affairs in Jing and Yu provinces.
units.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Taihe (227), the Son of Heaven ordered the emperor to garrison at Wan and additionally placed him in command of military affairs in Jing and Yu provinces.

units.zh: 初，蜀將孟達之降也，魏朝遇之甚厚。
units.en: Earlier, when Shu’s general Meng Da defected, Wei showered him with favor.
units.literal: Earlier, when Shu general Meng Da had surrendered, the Wei court treated him generously.

units.zh: 帝以達言行傾巧不可任，驟諫不見聽，乃以達領新城太守，封侯，假節。
units.en: He judged Da’s tongue treacherous and untrustworthy; repeated remonstrance failed, so Da received acting prefect of Xincheng, a marquisate, and the credential axe.
units.literal: The Emperor deemed Da’s words and conduct slippery and unreliable; though he remonstrated repeatedly he was not heard, and Da was made acting prefect of Xincheng, enfeoffed as a marquis, and given the ceremonial axe.

units.zh: 達於是連吳固蜀，潛圖中國。
units.en: Da then stitched Wu to Shu and schemed against the heartland in secret.
units.literal: Da then allied with Wu and Shu and secretly plotted against the central plains.

units.zh: 蜀相諸葛亮惡其反覆，又慮其為患。
units.en: Zhuge Liang despised his flip-flopping and dreaded the chaos he might unleash.
units.literal: Shu’s chancellor Zhuge Liang despised his vacillation and also feared he would cause trouble.

units.zh: 達與魏興太守申儀有隙，亮欲促其事，乃遣郭模詐降，過儀，因漏泄其謀。
units.en: Da quarrelled with Shen Yi of Weixing; Liang hurried matters by sending Guo Mo under false colors past Yi to spill the conspiracy.
units.literal: Da had a rift with Shen Yi, prefect of Weixing; Liang wished to hasten matters and sent Guo Mo feigning surrender, who passed through Yi and leaked the plot.

units.zh: 達聞其謀漏泄，將舉兵。
units.en: Once Da learned the secret was out, he prepared to rebel.
units.literal: When Da heard his plot had leaked, he prepared to rise in arms.

units.zh: 帝恐達速發，以書喻之曰：「將軍昔棄劉備，託身國家，國家委將軍以疆埸之任，任將軍以圖蜀之事，可謂心貫白日。
units.en: Fearing a swift rising, he wrote: “You abandoned Liu Bei for us; we placed the border in your hands and tasked you with Shu—your loyalty blazes like noon.
units.literal: The Emperor feared Da would move quickly and wrote to him: “General, you once abandoned Liu Bei and entrusted yourself to the state; the state entrusted you with the frontier and charged you with planning against Shu—your heart may be said to pierce the bright sun.

units.zh: 蜀人愚智，莫不切齒於將軍。
units.en: Every Shu soul, wise or dull, grinds teeth at your name.
units.literal: Wise or foolish, everyone in Shu gnashes teeth at you.

units.zh: 諸葛亮欲相破，惟苦無路耳。
units.en: Zhuge Liang longs to ruin you yet lacked a lever until now.
units.literal: Zhuge Liang wishes to destroy you but only lacks the means.

units.zh: 模之所言，非小事也，亮豈輕之而令宣露，此殆易知耳。」
units.en: Mo’s tale is no gossip—would Zhuge Liang broadcast it carelessly? The answer is plain.”
units.literal: What Mo said is no trifle—would Liang treat it lightly and let it spread? This is easy to see.”

units.zh: 達得書大喜，猶與不決。
units.en: Da read the letter with delight yet still wavered.
units.literal: Da received the letter and was greatly pleased, yet still hesitated.

units.zh: 帝乃潛軍進討。
units.en: He then stole forward with the army.
units.literal: The Emperor then secretly advanced to attack.

units.zh: 諸將言達與二賊交構，宜觀望而後動。
units.en: His officers argued Da colluded with both enemies and urged caution.
units.literal: The generals said Da was in league with the two foes and they should watch and wait before acting.

units.zh: 帝曰：「達無信義，此其相疑之時也，當及其未定促決之。」
units.en: He said, “Da knows no loyalty—this is the hour of mutual doubt; strike before his camp steadies.”
units.literal: The Emperor said, “Da lacks good faith; this is when mutual suspicion reigns—we must strike before he is settled.”

units.zh: 乃倍道兼行，八日到其城下。
units.en: He forced the march and reached the walls in eight days.
units.literal: He therefore doubled the march and in eight days reached the walls.

units.zh: 吳蜀各遣其將向西城安橋、木闌塞以救達，帝分諸將以距之。
units.en: Wu and Shu each rushed columns toward Xicheng, An Bridge, and Mulansai to rescue Da; he split commands to intercept them.
units.literal: Wu and Shu each sent generals toward Xicheng, Anqiao, and Mulansai to relieve Da; the Emperor divided his generals to block them.

units.zh: 初，達與亮書曰：「宛去洛八百里，去吾一千二百里，聞吾舉事，當表上天子，比相反覆，一月間也，則吾城已固，諸軍足辦。
units.en: Da once wrote Zhuge Liang: “Wan lies eight hundred li from Luoyang and twelve hundred from me; were I to rebel, Luoyang must memorialize the throne—round-trip paperwork eats a month; by then my walls would stand firm and my troops ready.
units.literal: Earlier Da had written to Liang: “Wan is eight hundred li from Luoyang and twelve hundred from me; when I rise, [the court] must memorialize the Son of Heaven—by the time reports go back and forth a month will have passed; then my city will be secure and my forces ready.

units.zh: 則吾所在深險，司馬公必不自來；
units.en: My terrain is rugged and remote—Lord Sima will never march in person;
units.literal: My position is deep and defensible; Lord Sima will surely not come himself;

units.zh: 諸將來，吾無患矣。」
units.en: if only subordinates arrive I need not worry.”
units.literal: if only his generals come, I have nothing to fear.”

units.zh: 及兵到，達又告亮曰：「吾舉事八日，而兵至城下，何其神速也！」
units.en: When the army appeared Da wired Liang: “Eight days into my rising and they ring my walls—what speed!”
units.literal: When the troops arrived, Da told Liang: “I rose eight days ago and already troops are at my walls—how swift!”

units.zh: 上庸城三面阻水，達於城外為木柵以自固。
units.en: Shangyong hugged water on three faces; Da threw up timber palisades beyond the walls.
units.literal: Shangyong was bounded by water on three sides; Da built a wooden palisade outside the city to fortify himself.

units.zh: [3]帝渡水，破其柵，直造城下。
units.en: [3] He forded the streams, smashed the stockade, and drove to the moat.
units.literal: [3] The Emperor crossed the water, broke the palisade, and came straight to the foot of the walls.

units.zh: 八道攻之，旬有六日，達甥鄧賢、將李輔等開門出降。
units.en: He assaulted along eight avenues; sixteen days later Deng Xian the nephew and general Li Fu opened the gates and capitulated.
units.literal: He attacked from eight directions; after sixteen days Deng Xian, Da’s nephew, and general Li Fu and others opened the gates and surrendered.

units.zh: 斬達，傳首京師。
units.en: They beheaded Meng Da and forwarded his head to Luoyang.
units.literal: Da was executed and his head sent to the capital.

units.zh: 俘獲萬餘人，振旅還于宛。
units.en: They took over ten thousand prisoners and marched back to Wan with drums beating.
units.literal: More than ten thousand captives were taken; the army marched back to Wan in good order.

units.zh: 乃勸農桑，禁浮費，南土悅附焉。
units.en: He urged tillage and silk production, banned needless expense, and the south rallied to him willingly.
units.literal: He then promoted farming and sericulture, forbade wasteful spending, and the southern lands gladly submitted.

units.zh: 初，申儀久在魏興，專威疆埸，輒承制刻印，多所假授。
units.en: Shen Yi had dominated Weixing for years—running the border like a private fief, minting seals without sanction, and handing out titles at will.
units.literal: Earlier, Shen Yi had long held Weixing, arrogated authority along the frontier, repeatedly carved seals on his own authority, and handed out many irregular appointments.

units.zh: 達既誅，有自疑心。
units.en: Once Meng Da fell, Shen Yi began to doubt his own safety.
units.literal: After Da was put to death, Yi grew suspicious of his own position.

units.zh: 時諸郡守以帝新克捷，奉禮求賀，皆聽之。
units.en: County governors arrived with congratulations on his fresh triumph; he received every delegation.
units.literal: At that time the various prefects, because the Emperor had just won a victory, brought gifts seeking congratulation; he accepted them all.

units.zh: 帝使人諷儀，儀至，問承制狀，執之，歸于京師。
units.en: He hinted until Shen Yi appeared at audience, pressed him on those self-made commissions, arrested him, and shipped him east.
units.literal: The Emperor sent someone to sound out Yi; when Yi came to court he questioned him about his unauthorized appointments, seized him, and sent him to the capital.

units.zh: 又徙孟達餘眾七千餘家於幽州。
units.en: He resettled over seven thousand surviving households of Meng Da’s remnant followers in Youzhou.
units.literal: He also relocated more than seven thousand households of Meng Da’s remnant followers to Youzhou.

units.zh: 蜀將姚靜、鄭他等帥其屬七千餘人來降。
units.en: Yao Jing and Zheng Ta of Shu marched in over seven thousand troops to defect.
units.literal: Shu generals Yao Jing and Zheng Ta led their followers—more than seven thousand men—to surrender.

units.zh: 時邊郡新附，多無戶名，魏朝欲加隱實。
units.en: The newly subdued border prefectures still lacked proper household rolls, and the court meant to audit them.
units.literal: At that time the newly annexed marches often lacked registered households, and the Wei court wished to verify them thoroughly.

units.zh: 屬帝朝於京師，天子訪之於帝。
units.en: While he was at audience in Luoyang, the emperor took him aside for advice.
units.literal: When the Emperor attended court in the capital, the Son of Heaven consulted him on the matter.

units.zh: 帝對曰：「賊以密網束下，故下棄之。
units.en: He answered: “Bandits rule through a thousand petty regulations—that is why their subjects flee.
units.literal: The Emperor replied: “The rebels bound their subjects with a harsh net, so the people abandoned them.

units.zh: 宜弘以大綱，則自然安樂。」
units.en: Govern with a loose rein and calm follows without forcing it.”
units.literal: You should rule with a broad policy; then peace will come of itself.”

units.zh: 又問二虜宜討，何者為先？
units.en: The sovereign then asked which foe—Wu or Shu—should come first.
units.literal: He was also asked which of the two enemies ought to be attacked first.

units.zh: 對曰：「吳以中國不習水戰，故敢散居東關。
units.en: He said: “Wu gambles that we fear naval combat, so they string their lines along the eastern passes.
units.literal: He replied: “Wu presumes that the Central Plains do not excel at river warfare, which is why they dare scatter their forces along Dongguan.

units.zh: 凡攻敵，必扼其喉而摏其心。
units.en: Strike always at throat and heart—that is how wars are won.
units.literal: In every attack on an enemy one must seize his throat and strike his heart.

units.zh: 夏口、東關，賊之心喉。
units.en: Xiakou and Dongguan are precisely those vital points.
units.literal: Xiakou and Dongguan are that foe’s heart and throat.

units.zh: 若為陸軍以向皖城，引權東下，為水戰軍向夏口，乘其虛而擊之，此神兵從天而墮，破之必矣。」
units.en: Send infantry toward Wancheng to tug Sun Quan downstream while your fleet thrusts at Xiakou and catches him thin—that is an assault from heaven itself.”
units.literal: If you march a field army toward Wancheng and draw Sun Quan eastward, while a river force pushes toward Xiakou and hits him where he is weak, it will be like heavenly troops falling from the sky—you will surely break him.”

units.zh: 天子並然之，復命帝屯於宛。
units.en: The emperor endorsed it wholeheartedly and told him once more to hold Wan.
units.literal: The Son of Heaven deeply approved and again ordered the Emperor to encamp at Wan.

units.zh: 四年，遷大將軍，加大都督、假黃鉞，與曹真伐蜀。
units.en: Fourth year: he became Grand General and supreme commander with the yellow axe, campaigning beside Cao Zhen against Shu.
units.literal: In the fourth year he was promoted to Grand General, invested as supreme commander-in-chief with the yellow battle-axe, and joined Cao Zhen in campaigning against Shu.

units.zh: 帝自西城斫山開道，水陸並進，泝沔而上，至於朐䏰，拔其新豐縣。
units.en: He hacked a route from Xicheng, drove land and river columns up the Han to Quyu, and seized Xinfeng County.
units.literal: From Xicheng he cut roads through the mountains and advanced by land and water together, moving up the Han River as far as Quyu, where he took Xinfeng County.

units.zh: 軍次丹口，遇雨，班師。
units.en: They paused at Dankou until storms forced a withdrawal.
units.literal: The army halted at Dankou; rain fell and he ordered the troops withdrawn.

units.zh: 明年，諸葛亮寇天水，圍將軍賈嗣、魏平於祁山。
units.en: Next year Zhuge Liang struck Tianshui and penned Jia Si and Wei Ping inside Qishan.
units.literal: The following year Zhuge Liang raided Tianshui and besieged Generals Jia Si and Wei Ping at Qishan.

units.zh: 天子曰：「西方有事，非君莫可付者。」
units.en: The Son of Heaven said: “Only you can shoulder the western front.”
units.literal: The Son of Heaven said: “The west is in crisis—there is no one else I can entrust.”

units.zh: 乃使帝西屯長安，都督雍、梁二州諸軍事，[4]統車騎將軍張郃、後將軍費曜、征蜀護軍戴淩、雍州刺史郭淮等討亮。
units.en: So the Son of Heaven sent the Emperor west to camp at Chang’an as commander for Yong and Liang, directing Zhang He, Fei Yao, Dai Ling, Guo Huai, and the rest against Zhuge Liang.
units.literal: He therefore sent the Emperor to camp west at Chang’an with overall command of Yong and Liang provinces [4] and leadership over General of Chariots and Cavalry Zhang He, General of the Rear Fei Yao, Protector of the Army for the Shu Campaign Dai Ling, Inspector of Yongzhou Guo Huai, and others against Zhuge Liang.

units.zh: 張郃勸帝分軍住雍、郿為後鎮，帝曰：「料前軍獨能當之者，將軍言是也。
units.en: Zhang He proposed splitting forces between Yong and Mei as a reserve; he replied: “If the van can carry the fight alone, you are correct.
units.literal: Zhang He urged the Emperor to divide the army and station part at Yong and Mei as a rear guard; the Emperor said: “If you judge that the van alone can hold him, general, you speak rightly.

units.zh: 若不能當，而分為前後，此楚之三軍所以為黥布禽也。」
units.en: Split them while the front fails and you repeat Chu’s disaster at Qing Bu’s hands.”
units.literal: But if it cannot hold and you split front from rear, that is how Chu’s three armies came to be captured by Qing Bu.”

units.zh: 遂進軍隃麋。
units.en: He pushed on to Yumi.
units.literal: He therefore advanced to Yumi.

units.zh: 亮聞大軍且至，乃自帥眾將芟上邽之麥。
units.en: Hearing the host approach, Zhuge Liang himself crossed into Shanggui to strip the wheat fields.
units.literal: When Liang learned that the main army was approaching, he personally led his troops to reap the wheat at Shanggui.

units.zh: 諸將皆懼，帝曰：「亮慮多決少，必安營自固，然後芟麥，吾得二日兼行足矣。」
units.en: The generals were all afraid. The emperor said, "Liang is full of anxieties and makes few decisions; he will certainly secure his camp first and only afterward cut the wheat. Two days of forced marching will be enough for me."
units.literal: The generals were all afraid. The emperor said, "Liang is full of anxieties and makes few decisions; he will certainly secure his camp first and only afterward cut the wheat. Two days of forced marching will be enough for me."

units.zh: 於是卷甲晨夜赴之，亮望塵而遁。
units.en: They shed baggage and ran nonstop; Zhuge Liang bolted at their dust cloud.
units.literal: Thereupon they rolled up armor and raced day and night; Liang fled at the sight of their dust.

units.zh: 帝曰：「吾倍道疲勞，此曉兵者之所貪也。
units.en: He said: “Fatigue from speed is what seasoned troops crave.
units.literal: The Emperor said: “We have exhausted ourselves on a forced march—exactly what an army that understands war covets.

units.zh: 亮不敢據渭水，此易與耳。」
units.en: He will not anchor on the Wei—he is ours to manage.”
units.literal: Liang dare not hold the Wei River—he will be easy to handle.”

units.zh: 進次漢陽，與亮相遇，帝列陣以待之。
units.en: He moved into Hanyang, met Zhuge Liang, and formed front against him.
units.literal: He advanced to Hanyang, encountered Liang, and drew up battle lines to await him.

units.zh: 使將牛金輕騎餌之，兵才接而亮退，追至祁山。
units.en: Niu Jin’s light horse drew him out; after a brush Zhuge Liang ran and they chased all the way to Qishan.
units.literal: He ordered General Niu Jin with light cavalry to bait him; scarcely had the lines engaged when Liang withdrew, and they pursued to Qishan.

units.zh: 亮屯鹵城，據南北二山，斷水為重圍。
units.en: Zhuge Liang walled up Lucheng between two ridges and ringed himself with cut rivers.
units.literal: Liang encamped at Lucheng, holding the northern and southern hills and cutting off the water to build layered defenses.

units.zh: 帝攻拔其圍，亮宵遁，追擊破之，俘斬萬計。
units.en: He smashed the rings; Zhuge Liang fled by dark and was chased down—dead and captured beyond count.
units.literal: The Emperor stormed and broke his fortifications; Liang slipped away by night, was pursued and defeated, and tens of thousands were killed or captured.

units.zh: 天子使使者勞軍，增封邑。
units.en: Imperial envoys brought rewards and added to his appanage.
units.literal: The Son of Heaven dispatched envoys to reward the army and enlarged his fief.

units.zh: 時軍師杜襲、督軍薛悌皆言明年麥熟，亮必為寇，隴右無穀，宜及冬豫運。
units.en: Du Xi and Xue Ti warned that next harvest Zhuge Liang would return while Longyou starved—haul grain before winter.
units.literal: At that time army adviser Du Xi and supervisor Xue Ti both said that when the wheat ripened the next year Liang would surely raid again; Longyou lacked grain and supplies ought to be moved before winter.

units.zh: 帝曰：「亮再出祁山，一攻陳倉，挫衄而反。
units.en: He answered: “Twice from Qishan, once at Chencang—each time repulsed.
units.literal: The Emperor said: “Liang has twice emerged from Qishan and once assaulted Chencang—each time he was beaten back.

units.zh: 縱其後出，不復攻城，當求野戰，必在隴東，不在西也。
units.en: Next time he will hunt open battle east of the Long ridges, not west.
units.literal: Even if he comes out again he will not storm cities; he will seek a field battle east of Long, not west.

units.zh: 亮每以糧少為恨，歸必積穀，以吾料之，非三稔不能動矣。」
units.en: Grain gnaws at him—every retreat piles granaries. He cannot march for three full crops.”
units.literal: Liang always lamented his shortage of grain; whenever he withdrew he stockpiled—by my reckoning he cannot move for three harvests.”

units.zh: 於是表徙冀州農夫佃上邽，興京兆、天水、南安監冶。
units.en: He filed to transplant Ji farmers onto Shanggui fields and to tool imperial armories in Jingzhao, Tianshui, and Nan’an.
units.literal: He therefore memorialized to move tenant farmers from Ji Province up to Shanggui and to establish government foundries in Jingzhao, Tianshui, and Nan’an.

units.zh: 青龍元年，穿成國渠，築臨晉陂，溉田數千頃，國以充實焉。
units.en: In the first year of Qinglong (233), he dug and completed the Guo Canal and built the Linjin embankment, irrigating several thousand qing of fields, and the state thereby became full and prosperous.
units.literal: In the first year of Qinglong (233), he dug and completed the Guo Canal and built the Linjin embankment, irrigating several thousand qing of fields, and the state thereby became full and prosperous.

units.zh: 二年，亮又率眾十餘萬出斜谷，壘于郿之渭水南原。
units.en: Year two: Zhuge Liang drove a hundred thousand through Xie Valley and dug in south of the Wei at Mei.
units.literal: In the second year Liang again led more than a hundred thousand men out of Xie Valley and fortified the southern bank of the Wei south of Mei.

units.zh: 天子憂之，遣征蜀護軍秦朗督步騎二萬，受帝節度。
units.en: The throne detached Qin Lang with twenty thousand foot and horse under his orders.
units.literal: The Son of Heaven was troubled and sent Protector of the Army for the Shu Campaign Qin Lang with twenty thousand infantry and cavalry to operate under the Emperor’s direction.

units.zh: 諸將欲住渭北以待之，帝曰：「百姓積聚皆在渭南，此必爭之地也。」
units.en: The generals wanted to stay north of the Wei and wait for him. The emperor said, "The people's stores are all south of the Wei; this is certainly ground that will be contested."
units.literal: The generals wanted to stay north of the Wei and wait for him. The emperor said, "The people's stores are all south of the Wei; this is certainly ground that will be contested."

units.zh: 遂引軍而濟，背水為壘。
units.en: He crossed and stacked camps against the water.
units.literal: He therefore led the army across and built ramparts with the river at his back.

units.zh: 因謂諸將曰：「亮若勇者，當出武功，依山而東。
units.en: He lectured them: “A daring Zhuge Liang would burst from Wugong along the ridges east.
units.literal: He told the generals: “If Liang were bold he would exit through Wugong and wheel east along the hills.

units.zh: 若西上五丈原，則諸軍無事矣。」
units.en: If he climbs Wuzhangyuan westward we may barely need to stir.”
units.literal: If instead he climbs Wuzhangyuan to the west, our armies may stand idle.”

units.zh: 亮果上原，將北渡渭，帝遣將軍周當屯陽遂以餌之。
units.en: Zhuge Liang did march onto the plateau and line up a northern crossing; Zhou Dang feigned at Yangsui.
units.literal: Liang indeed climbed the plateau and prepared to cross the Wei northward; the Emperor sent General Zhou Dang to hold Yangsui as bait.

units.zh: 數日，亮不動。
units.en: Days passed without Zhuge Liang stirring.
units.literal: Several days passed and Liang did not move.

units.zh: 帝曰：「亮欲爭原而不向陽遂，此意可知也。」
units.en: The emperor said, "Liang wants to contest the plain and is not heading toward Yangsui; his intention can be known."
units.literal: The emperor said, "Liang wants to contest the plain and is not heading toward Yangsui; his intention can be known."

units.zh: 遣將軍胡遵、雍州剌史郭淮共備陽遂，與亮會于積石。
units.en: Hu Zun and Guo Huai sealed Yangsui and met Zhuge Liang at Jishi.
units.literal: He dispatched Generals Hu Zun and Inspector of Yongzhou Guo Huai jointly to secure Yangsui, and they joined Liang at Jishi.

units.zh: 臨原而戰，亮不得進，還於五丈原。
units.en: Combat along the heights stalled Zhuge Liang and drove him back to Wuzhangyuan.
units.literal: They fought along the edge of the plateau; Liang could not advance and withdrew to Wuzhangyuan.

units.zh: 會有長星墜亮之壘，帝知其必敗，遣奇兵掎亮之後，斬五百餘級，獲生口千餘，降者六百餘人。
units.en: A comet struck Zhuge Liang’s camp—proof of doom—so raiders hit his rear: five hundred heads, a thousand prisoners, six hundred who yielded.
units.literal: When a long comet fell on Liang’s camp the Emperor knew he was doomed; he sent unexpected troops to strike Liang’s rear, beheaded more than five hundred, captured over a thousand alive, and accepted six hundred surrenders.

units.zh: 時朝廷以亮僑軍遠寇，利在急戰，每命帝持重，以候其變。
units.en: Court opinion held that a distant expedition favored a quick battle; orders told him to remain cautious and wait for a shift.
units.literal: At that time the court held that Liang’s army was an expeditionary force operating far from home and favored forcing a quick battle; each time it ordered the Emperor to remain cautious and wait for a shift.

units.zh: 亮數挑戰，帝不出，因遺帝巾幗婦人之飾。
units.en: Zhuge Liang baited him repeatedly; he stayed quiet until women’s kerchiefs arrived.
units.literal: Liang repeatedly challenged him to battle; the Emperor would not emerge, so Liang sent him women’s scarves and headbands as taunts.

units.zh: 帝怒，表請決戰，天子不許，乃遣骨鯁臣衞尉辛毗杖節為軍師以制之。
units.en: The Emperor angrily memorialized for a decisive battle; the Son of Heaven refused and posted Xin Pi with staff authority to restrain him.
units.literal: The Emperor angrily memorialized for a decisive engagement; the Son of Heaven forbade it and instead sent the blunt Captain of the Gate Xin Pi with imperial insignia as army adviser to restrain him.

units.zh: 後亮復來挑戰，帝將出兵以應之，毗杖節立軍門，帝乃止。
units.en: When Zhuge Liang tried again he nearly rode out—Xin Pi blocked the gate with his baton until he stopped.
units.literal: Later when Liang challenged again the Emperor was about to march out to answer; Xin Pi stood staff-in-hand at the camp gate and he desisted.

units.zh: 初，蜀將姜維聞毗來，謂亮曰：「辛毗杖節而至，賊不復出矣。」
units.en: Jiang Wei had warned: “Xin Pi means no more field battles.”
units.literal: Earlier, when Shu general Jiang Wei heard that Xin Pi had come, he told Liang: “Xin Pi arrives with credentials—the enemy will not come forth again.”

units.zh: 亮曰：「彼本無戰心，所以固請者，以示武于其眾耳。
units.en: Zhuge Liang answered: “They seek spectacle, not steel—they parade martial theater for the ranks.
units.literal: Liang said: “They have no real wish to fight; their insistence on requesting battle is only to put martial spirit on display before their troops.

units.zh: 將在軍，君命有所不受，苟能制吾，豈千里而請戰邪！」
units.en: Field commanders ignore distant edicts—if they could trap me they would not request battle from a thousand li away!”
units.literal: A general in the field may reject orders from his ruler; if they could truly pin me down, why would they memorialize for battle from a thousand li away!”

units.zh: 帝弟孚書問軍事，帝復書曰：「亮志大而不見機，多謀而少決，好兵而無權，雖提卒十萬，巳墮吾畫中，破之必矣。」
units.en: The emperor's younger brother Fu wrote to ask about military affairs, and the emperor replied, "Liang has great ambitions but does not see opportunity, makes many plans but few decisions, loves warfare but has no flexibility. Although he leads one hundred thousand soldiers, he has already fallen into my design, and I will certainly defeat him."
units.literal: The emperor's younger brother Fu wrote to ask about military affairs, and the emperor replied, "Liang has great ambitions but does not see opportunity, makes many plans but few decisions, loves warfare but has no flexibility. Although he leads one hundred thousand soldiers, he has already fallen into my design, and I will certainly defeat him."

units.zh: 與之對壘百餘日，會亮病卒，諸將燒營遁走，百姓奔告，帝出兵追之。
units.en: A hundred days of stalemate ended when Zhuge Liang died—his men torched camp and bolted, civilians brought word, and pursuit followed.
units.literal: After opposing him for more than a hundred days, Liang died of illness; his generals burned the camps and fled, the people ran to report it, and the Emperor sent troops in pursuit.

units.zh: 亮長史楊儀反旗鳴鼓，若將距帝者。
units.en: Yang Yi feigned a counterattack—flags reversed, drums thundering.
units.literal: Liang’s chief clerk Yang Yi reversed the banners and beat the drums as if preparing to resist the Emperor.

units.zh: 帝以窮寇不之逼，於是楊儀結陣而去。
units.en: He refused to harry a desperate foe, so Yang Yi marched away in order.
units.literal: The Emperor would not press a cornered enemy; Yang Yi therefore formed ranks and withdrew.

units.zh: 經日，乃行其營壘，觀其遺事，獲其圖書、糧穀甚眾。
units.en: Next day he walked the abandoned works and seized maps, papers, and grain in heaps.
units.literal: After a full day he entered their fortifications, inspected what they had left behind, and captured a great quantity of maps, documents, and grain.

units.zh: 帝審其必死，曰：「天下奇才也。」
units.en: The emperor judged that he must have died and said, "He was a rare talent under Heaven."
units.literal: The emperor judged that he must have died and said, "He was a rare talent under Heaven."

units.zh: 辛毗以為尚未可知。
units.en: Xin Pi still urged caution.
units.literal: Xin Pi thought the matter still uncertain.

units.zh: 帝曰：「軍家所重，軍書密計、兵馬糧穀，今皆棄之，豈有人捐其五藏而可以生乎？
units.en: The emperor said, "What military men value are military documents, secret plans, troops, horses, grain, and provisions. Now all of these have been abandoned. How could someone cast away his five viscera and still live?
units.literal: The emperor said, "What military men value are military documents, secret plans, troops, horses, grain, and provisions. Now all of these have been abandoned. How could someone cast away his five viscera and still live?

units.zh: 宜急追之。」
units.en: We should pursue him urgently."
units.literal: We should pursue him urgently."

units.zh: 關中多蒺䔧，帝使軍士二千人著軟材平底木屐前行，蒺藜悉著屐，然後馬步俱進。
units.en: Guanzhong bristled with caltrops—two thousand men in wooden clogs swept the path clear for horse and foot.
units.literal: Guanzhong was thick with caltrops; the Emperor had two thousand soldiers put on soft wooden clogs with flat soles and walk ahead; the caltrops stuck to the clogs, after which cavalry and infantry advanced together.

units.zh: 追到赤岸，乃知亮死審問。
units.en: Only at Red Shore did rumor harden into fact.
units.literal: They pursued to Red Shore (Chì’àn) and only then confirmed beyond doubt that Liang was dead.

units.zh: 時百姓為之諺曰：「死諸葛走生仲達。」
units.en: People sang: “The dead Zhuge ran off the living Zhongda.”
units.literal: The common folk composed a rhyme: “A dead Zhuge drove off a living Zhongda.”

units.zh: 帝聞而笑曰：「吾便料生，不便料死故也。」
units.en: He laughed: “I could read him breathing; I could not read him cold—that was my blind spot.”
units.literal: When the Emperor heard it he laughed and said: “I could judge him alive; I could not judge him dead—that is all.”

units.zh: 先是，亮使至，帝問曰：「諸葛公起居何如，食可幾米？」
units.en: Before this, when Liang's envoy arrived, the emperor asked, "How is Zhuge Gong doing in rising, resting, and daily life? How many sheng of rice can he eat?"
units.literal: Before this, when Liang's envoy arrived, the emperor asked, "How is Zhuge Gong doing in rising, resting, and daily life? How many sheng of rice can he eat?"

units.zh: 對曰：「三四升。」
units.en: He replied, "Three or four sheng."
units.literal: He replied, "Three or four sheng."

units.zh: 次問政事，曰：「二十罰已上皆自省覽。」
units.en: He next asked about government affairs, and the envoy said, "He personally reviews all punishments of twenty strokes and above."
units.literal: He next asked about government affairs, and the envoy said, "He personally reviews all punishments of twenty strokes and above."

units.zh: 帝既而告人曰：「諸葛孔明其能久乎！」
units.en: The emperor afterward told others, "Can Zhuge Kongming last long?"
units.literal: The emperor afterward told others, "Can Zhuge Kongming last long?"

units.zh: 竟如其言。
units.en: Time proved him right.
units.literal: Events proved him right.

units.zh: 亮部將楊儀、魏延爭權，儀斬延，并其眾。
units.en: Yang Yi murdered Wei Yan and seized his command.
units.literal: Liang’s officers Yang Yi and Wei Yan struggled for power; Yi executed Yan and absorbed his troops.

units.zh: 帝欲乘隙而進，有詔不許。
units.en: He itched to strike the chaos; an imperial veto stopped him.
units.literal: The Emperor wished to exploit the opening and advance, but an edict forbade it.

units.zh: 三年，遷太尉，累增封邑。
units.en: Third year: Grand Commandant, with fiefs piled higher.
units.literal: In the third year he was promoted to Grand Commandant and his fief was repeatedly enlarged.

units.zh: 蜀將馬岱入寇，帝遣將軍牛金擊走之，斬千餘級。
units.en: Ma Dai of Shu raided in; Niu Jin threw him back with a thousand heads.
units.literal: Shu general Ma Dai raided the border; the Emperor sent General Niu Jin to drive him off and beheaded more than a thousand.

units.zh: 武都氐王苻雙、強端帥其屬六千餘人來降。
units.en: Fu Shuang and Qiang Duan of Wudu Di brought six thousand followers in.
units.literal: The Di kings of Wudu, Fu Shuang and Qiang Duan, led more than six thousand of their followers to surrender.

units.en: Six.
units.literal: Six.

units.zh: 關東饑，帝運長安粟五百萬斛輸於京師。
units.en: Famine east of the passes—five million hu moved from Chang’an to Luoyang.
units.literal: East of the passes suffered famine; the Emperor shipped five million hu of grain from Chang’an to the capital.

units.zh: 四年，獲白鹿，獻之。
units.en: Fourth year: hunters presented a white deer.
units.literal: In the fourth year a white deer was captured and presented.

units.zh: 天子曰：「昔周公旦輔成王，有素雉之貢。
units.en: The Son of Heaven said, "In the past, when the Duke of Zhou assisted King Cheng, there was tribute of a white pheasant.
units.literal: The Son of Heaven said, "In the past, when the Duke of Zhou assisted King Cheng, there was tribute of a white pheasant.

units.zh: 今君受陝西之任，有白鹿之獻，豈非忠誠協符，千載同契，俾乂邦家，以永厥休邪！」
units.en: Now you have received the responsibility for Shaanxi, and there has been an offering of a white deer. Is this not loyal sincerity matching the sign, the same accord across a thousand years, causing the state and house to be well governed and forever extending its blessing?"
units.literal: Now you have received the responsibility for Shaanxi, and there has been an offering of a white deer. Is this not loyal sincerity matching the sign, the same accord across a thousand years, causing the state and house to be well governed and forever extending its blessing?"

units.zh: 及遼東太守公孫文懿反，徵帝詣京師。
units.en: Gongsun Yuan’s revolt pulled him to Luoyang.
units.literal: When Liaodong Prefect Gongsun Yuan rebelled, the Emperor was summoned to the capital.

units.zh: 天子曰：「此不足以勞君，事欲必克，故以相煩耳。
units.en: The Son of Heaven said, "This is not enough to trouble you, but the affair must certainly be won, and therefore I bother you with it.
units.literal: The Son of Heaven said, "This is not enough to trouble you, but the affair must certainly be won, and therefore I bother you with it.

units.zh: 君度其作何計？」
units.en: What plan do you think he will make?"
units.literal: What plan do you think he will make?"

units.zh: 對曰：「棄城預走，上計也。
units.en: He replied, "To abandon the city and flee in advance would be the best plan.
units.literal: He replied, "To abandon the city and flee in advance would be the best plan.

units.zh: 據遼水以距大軍，次計也。
units.en: Middle course: defend the Liao line.
units.literal: Hold the Liao River to block the main army—that is the middling plan.

units.zh: 坐守襄平，此成擒耳。」
units.en: To sit and guard Xiangping means he is already captured."
units.literal: To sit and guard Xiangping means he is already captured."

units.zh: 天子曰：「其計將安出？」
units.en: The Son of Heaven said, "Where will his plan come out?"
units.literal: The Son of Heaven said, "Where will his plan come out?"

units.zh: 對曰：「惟明者能深度彼己，豫有所棄，此非其所及也。
units.en: He replied, "Only an enlightened man can deeply measure both enemy and self and abandon something in advance; this is beyond him.
units.literal: He replied, "Only an enlightened man can deeply measure both enemy and self and abandon something in advance; this is beyond him.

units.zh: 今懸軍遠征，將謂不能持久，必先距遼水而後守，此中下計也。」
units.en: Now that our suspended army is campaigning far away, he will think we cannot last long and will surely first resist at the Liao River and only afterward defend; this is a middle-to-lower plan."
units.literal: Now that our suspended army is campaigning far away, he will think we cannot last long and will surely first resist at the Liao River and only afterward defend; this is a middle-to-lower plan."

units.zh: 天子曰：「往還幾時？」
units.en: The Son of Heaven said, "How long will the going and returning take?"
units.literal: The Son of Heaven said, "How long will the going and returning take?"

units.zh: 對曰：「往百日，還百日，攻百日，以六十日為休息，一年足矣。」
units.en: He answered: “March out a hundred days, come back a hundred, fight a hundred, rest sixty—that fills a year.”
units.literal: He replied: “Outbound one hundred days, return one hundred days, assault one hundred days, with sixty days set aside for rest—one year suffices.”

units.zh: 是時大修宮室，加之以軍旅，百姓饑弊。
units.en: Court architects ran wild while armies marched—the people starved under both burdens.
units.literal: At that time palace construction was greatly expanded and military campaigns piled on; the common people were hungry and exhausted.

units.zh: 帝將即戎，乃諫曰：「昔周公營洛邑，蕭何造未央，今宮室未備，臣之責也。
units.en: When the emperor was about to go to war, he remonstrated, saying, "In the past, the Duke of Zhou built Luoyi, and Xiao He built Weiyang. Now that the palace buildings are not yet complete, it is my responsibility.
units.literal: When the emperor was about to go to war, he remonstrated, saying, "In the past, the Duke of Zhou built Luoyi, and Xiao He built Weiyang. Now that the palace buildings are not yet complete, it is my responsibility.

units.zh: 然自河以北，百姓困窮，外內有役，勢不並興，宜假絕內務，以救時急。」
units.en: Yet north of the Yellow River, the people are impoverished; there are labor services both outside and inside, and the situation does not allow both to be undertaken at once. The inner works should be temporarily cut off, in order to save the current emergency."
units.literal: Yet north of the Yellow River, the people are impoverished; there are labor services both outside and inside, and the situation does not allow both to be undertaken at once. The inner works should be temporarily cut off, in order to save the current emergency."

units.zh: 景初二年，帥牛金、胡遵等步騎四萬，發自京都。
units.en: Jingchu year two: forty thousand horse and foot under Niu Jin and Hu Zun left Luoyang.
units.literal: In the second year of Jingchu (238) he led Niu Jin, Hu Zun, and others with forty thousand infantry and cavalry out of the capital.

units.zh: 車駕送出西明門，詔弟孚、子師送過溫，賜以穀帛牛酒，敕郡守典農以下皆往會焉。
units.en: The imperial carriage escorted him out through the Ximing Gate; an edict ordered his younger brother Fu and son Shi to see him past Wen, awarding grain, silk, cattle, and wine, and commanded the prefects and agricultural directors downward to assemble.
units.literal: The imperial carriage escorted him through the Ximing Gate; an edict ordered his younger brother Fu and son Shi to see him past Wen, awarding grain, silk, cattle, and wine, and commanded the prefect and agricultural director downward to assemble.

units.zh: 見父老故舊，讌飲累日。
units.en: He lingered with hometown elders over cups for night after night.
units.literal: He met elders and old friends and feasted for days on end.

units.zh: 帝歎息，悵然有感，為歌曰：「天地開闢，日月重光。
units.en: The emperor sighed and, moved with melancholy, made a song, saying, "Heaven and earth opened, sun and moon shone anew.
units.literal: The emperor sighed and, moved with melancholy, made a song, saying, "Heaven and earth opened, sun and moon shone anew.

units.zh: 遭遇際會，畢力遐方。
units.en: Encountering the moment of meeting, I spend all strength in distant regions.
units.literal: Encountering the moment of meeting, I spend all strength in distant regions.

units.zh: 將掃羣穢，還過故鄉。
units.en: I am about to sweep away the massed filth, and on return pass through my old home.
units.literal: I am about to sweep away the massed filth, and on return pass through my old home.

units.zh: 肅清萬里，總齊八荒。
units.en: Purifying ten thousand li, I shall gather and order the eight wastes.
units.literal: Purifying ten thousand li, I shall gather and order the eight wastes.

units.zh: 告成歸老，待罪舞陽。」
units.en: When success is reported, I will return old and await punishment at Wuyang."
units.literal: When success is reported, I will return old and await punishment at Wuyang."

units.zh: 遂進師，經孤竹，越碣石，次于遼水。
units.en: The columns rolled past Guzhu and Jieshi to the Liao.
units.literal: Thereupon he advanced the army, passed Guzhu, crossed Jieshi, and halted at the Liao River.

units.zh: 文懿果遣步騎數萬，阻遼隧，堅壁而守，南北六七十里，以距帝。
units.en: Gongsun Yuan plugged Liaosui with tens of thousands—palisades stretched seventy li along the narrows.
units.literal: Wenyi indeed sent several tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry to block Liaosui, fortifying walls and holding sixty or seventy li north to south against the Emperor.

units.zh: 帝盛兵多張旗幟出其南，賊盡銳赴之。
units.en: Sima Yi feigned strength on the southern bank and drew the Liaodong army off.
units.literal: The Emperor massed troops and unfurled many banners south of them; the rebels committed every elite regiment there.

units.zh: 乃泛舟潛濟以出其北，與賊營相逼，沈舟焚梁，傍遼水作長圍，棄賊而向襄平。
units.en: Under cover of dark water he slipped upstream, burned the crossings, pinned the Liao with earthworks, and ignored the camp for Xiangping.
units.literal: He then floated boats and secretly crossed to their north, pressing against their camp—sank boats, burned bridges, threw a long cordon along the Liao, abandoned the enemy column, and marched on Xiangping.

units.zh: 諸將言曰：「不攻賊而作圍，非所以示眾也。」
units.en: The generals said, "To make a siege without attacking the enemy is not the way to show resolve to the troops."
units.literal: The generals said, "To make a siege without attacking the enemy is not the way to show resolve to the troops."

units.zh: 帝曰：「賊堅營高壘，欲以老吾兵也。
units.en: The emperor said, "The enemy has made a firm camp and high ramparts because he wants to wear out our troops.
units.literal: The emperor said, "The enemy has made a firm camp and high ramparts because he wants to wear out our troops.

units.zh: 攻之，正入其計，此王邑所以恥過昆陽也。
units.en: If we attack it, we fall exactly into his plan; this is why Wang Yi was shamed at Kunyang.
units.literal: If we attack it, we fall exactly into his plan; this is why Wang Yi was shamed at Kunyang.

units.zh: 古人曰，敵雖高壘，不得不與我戰者，攻其所必救也。
units.en: The ancients said that even if the enemy has high ramparts, he cannot avoid fighting us if we attack what he must rescue.
units.literal: The ancients said that even if the enemy has high ramparts, he cannot avoid fighting us if we attack what he must rescue.

units.zh: 賊大眾在此，則巢窟虛矣。
units.en: The enemy's main force is here, so their nest is empty.
units.literal: The enemy's main force is here, so their nest is empty.

units.zh: 我直指襄平，則人懷內懼，懼而求戰，破之必矣。」
units.en: If I point straight at Xiangping, then the people will harbor internal fear; fearing, they will seek battle, and I will certainly defeat them."
units.literal: If I point straight at Xiangping, then the people will harbor internal fear; fearing, they will seek battle, and I will certainly defeat them."

units.zh: 遂整陣而過。
units.en: He aligned divisions and slipped past.
units.literal: Thereupon he dressed ranks and marched through.

units.zh: 賊見兵出其後，果邀之。
units.en: The Liaodong army wheeled about to cut him off.
units.literal: When the rebels saw troops emerge behind them they indeed tried to intercept.

units.zh: 帝謂諸將曰：「所以不攻其營，正欲致此，不可失也。」
units.en: The emperor told the generals, "The reason I did not attack their camp was precisely because I wanted to bring this about. We must not lose it."
units.literal: The emperor told the generals, "The reason I did not attack their camp was precisely because I wanted to bring this about. We must not lose it."

units.zh: 乃縱兵逆擊，大破之，三戰皆捷。
units.en: He hurled the lines forward and routed them thrice running.
units.literal: He then unleashed troops in a counterattack and shattered them; three engagements brought three victories.

units.zh: 賊保襄平，進軍圍之。
units.en: They fled inside Xiangping; he tightened the ring.
units.literal: The rebels held Xiangping; he advanced and invested it.

units.zh: 初，文懿聞魏師之出也，請救於孫權。
units.en: Gongsun Yuan had cried to Sun Quan when Wei stirred.
units.literal: Earlier, when Wenyi heard the Wei army had marched, he begged rescue from Sun Quan.

units.zh: 權亦出兵遙為之聲援，遺文懿書曰：「司馬公善用兵，變化若神，所向無前，深為弟憂之。」
units.en: Quan also sent troops from afar to make a show of support and sent Wenyì a letter, saying, "Sima Gong is good at using troops; his changes are like those of a spirit, and nothing stands before him wherever he turns. I am deeply worried for you, younger brother."
units.literal: Quan also sent troops from afar to make a show of support and sent Wenyì a letter, saying, "Sima Gong is good at using troops; his changes are like those of a spirit, and nothing stands before him wherever he turns. I am deeply worried for you, younger brother."

units.zh: 會霖潦，大水平地數尺，三軍恐，欲移營。
units.en: Monsoon floods drowned the plain; men clamored to move.
units.literal: Seasonal rains poured; floodwaters stood several chi deep on level ground; the three armies feared and wished to shift camp.

units.zh: 帝令軍中敢有言徙者斬。
units.en: He threatened death for talk of redeployment.
units.literal: The Emperor ordered that whoever spoke of relocating be executed.

units.zh: 都督令史張靜犯令，斬之，軍中乃定。
units.en: Zhang Jing broke the rule and lost his head—the ranks fell silent.
units.literal: Supervisory clerk Zhang Jing violated the order and was beheaded—only then did the army steady.

units.zh: 賊恃水，樵牧自若。
units.en: The defenders still sent out woodcutters as if dry.
units.literal: The rebels trusted the water and gathered firewood and grazed cattle as usual.

units.zh: 諸將欲取之，皆不聽。
units.en: Staff urged raids on foragers; he refused each time.
units.literal: The generals wished to seize those parties; he forbade every proposal.

units.zh: 司馬陳珪曰：「昔攻上庸，八部並進，晝夜不息，故能一旬之半，拔堅城，斬孟達。
units.en: Army officer Chen Gui said, "In the past, when we attacked Shangyong, eight divisions advanced together and did not rest day or night; therefore in half a ten-day period we were able to take a firm city and behead Meng Da.
units.literal: Army officer Chen Gui said, "In the past, when we attacked Shangyong, eight divisions advanced together and did not rest day or night; therefore in half a ten-day period we were able to take a firm city and behead Meng Da.

units.zh: 今者遠來而更安緩，愚竊惑焉。」
units.en: Now we have come from afar and instead are calm and slow; foolishly, I am privately puzzled by it."
units.literal: Now we have come from afar and instead are calm and slow; foolishly, I am privately puzzled by it."

units.zh: 帝曰：「孟達眾少而食支一年，吾將士四倍于達而糧不淹月，以一月圖一年，安可不速？
units.en: The emperor said, "Meng Da's men were few, and his food could support a year. My officers and soldiers are four times Da's, but our grain will not last a month. To plan for one year with one month, how could we not be quick?
units.literal: The emperor said, "Meng Da's men were few, and his food could support a year. My officers and soldiers are four times Da's, but our grain will not last a month. To plan for one year with one month, how could we not be quick?

units.zh: 以四擊一，正令半解，猶當為之。
units.en: Using four to attack one, even if half deserted, we still had to do it.
units.literal: Using four to attack one, even if half deserted, we still had to do it.

units.zh: 是以不計死傷，與糧競也。
units.en: For this reason we did not count death and injury; we were racing against grain.
units.literal: For this reason we did not count death and injury; we were racing against grain.

units.zh: 今賊眾我寡，賊飢我飽，水雨乃爾，功力不設，雖當促之，亦何所為。
units.en: Now the enemy is many and we are few; the enemy is hungry and we are full. With rain and water like this, works cannot be set up. Even if we should hurry him, what would it accomplish?
units.literal: Now the enemy is many and we are few; the enemy is hungry and we are full. With rain and water like this, works cannot be set up. Even if we should hurry him, what would it accomplish?

units.zh: 自發京師，不憂賊攻，但恐賊走。
units.en: Since leaving the capital, I have not worried that the enemy would attack; I only feared that the enemy would flee.
units.literal: Since leaving the capital, I have not worried that the enemy would attack; I only feared that the enemy would flee.

units.zh: 今賊糧垂盡，而圍落未合，掠其牛馬，抄其樵采，此故驅之走也。
units.en: Now the enemy's grain is nearly exhausted, but the encirclement is not complete. To seize his cattle and horses and raid his woodcutters and gatherers would deliberately drive him to flee.
units.literal: Now the enemy's grain is nearly exhausted, but the encirclement is not complete. To seize his cattle and horses and raid his woodcutters and gatherers would deliberately drive him to flee.

units.zh: 夫兵者詭道，善因事變。
units.en: War is the way of deception, and the skillful respond to changes in affairs.
units.literal: War is the way of deception, and the skillful respond to changes in affairs.

units.zh: 賊憑眾恃雨，故雖飢困，未肯束手，當示無能以安之。
units.en: The enemy relies on numbers and trusts to the rain; therefore, though hungry and distressed, he is not yet willing to bind his hands. We should show inability in order to reassure him.
units.literal: The enemy relies on numbers and trusts to the rain; therefore, though hungry and distressed, he is not yet willing to bind his hands. We should show inability in order to reassure him.

units.zh: 取小利以驚之。
units.en: To take small advantages and alarm him
units.literal: To take small advantages and alarm him

units.zh: 非計也。」
units.en: is not a plan."
units.literal: is not a plan."

units.zh: 朝廷聞師遇雨，咸請召還。
units.en: Luoyang heard mud and demanded withdrawal.
units.literal: The court heard the army met rain and all petitioned recall.

units.zh: 天子曰：「司馬公臨危制變，計日擒之矣。」
units.en: The Son of Heaven said, "Sima Gong controls change in the face of danger; he will capture him on the calculated day."
units.literal: The Son of Heaven said, "Sima Gong controls change in the face of danger; he will capture him on the calculated day."

units.zh: 既而雨止，遂合圍。
units.en: Skies cleared; the ring closed.
units.literal: Soon the rain stopped and they completed the cordon.

units.zh: 起土山地道，楯櫓鉤橦，發矢石雨下，晝夜攻之。
units.en: They stacked siege mounds, bored mines, and hailed stone until the walls shook.
units.literal: They piled earth hills and dug tunnels—shields, rams, hooks—arrows and stones rained in assault day and night.

units.zh: 時有長星，色白，有芒鬣，自襄平城西南流于東北，墜於梁水，城中震慴。
units.en: A white comet streaked from Xiangping’s southwest to the Liang—terror seized the town.
units.literal: At that time a long comet appeared, white with bristling rays, flowing from southwest of Xiangping toward northeast, falling into the Liang River—the city shook with terror.

units.zh: 文懿大懼，乃使其所署相國王建、御史大夫柳甫乞降，請解圍面縛。
units.en: Yuan sent Wang Jian and Liu Fu pleading for the siege to lift so he could come out with bound hands.
units.literal: Wenyi was terrified and sent his appointed Chancellor Wang Jian and Imperial Counselor Liu Fu to beg surrender, asking to lift the siege so he could bind himself.

units.zh: 不許，執建等，皆斬之。
units.en: Sima Yi refused—seized the envoys and took their heads.
units.literal: He did not consent—seized Jian and the others and executed them all.

units.zh: 檄告文懿曰：「昔楚鄭列國，而鄭伯猶肉袒牽羊而迎之。
units.en: A proclamation informed Wenyì, saying, "In the past, Chu and Zheng were ranked states, yet the Earl of Zheng still bared his flesh, led a sheep, and went out to meet Chu.
units.literal: A proclamation informed Wenyì, saying, "In the past, Chu and Zheng were ranked states, yet the Earl of Zheng still bared his flesh, led a sheep, and went out to meet Chu.

units.zh: 孤為王人，位則上公，而建等欲孤解圍退舍，豈楚鄭之謂邪！
units.en: I am a man of the king, and my rank is that of an upper duke, yet Jian and the others wanted me to lift the siege and withdraw. Is this what was meant by Chu and Zheng?
units.literal: I am a man of the king, and my rank is that of an upper duke, yet Jian and the others wanted me to lift the siege and withdraw. Is this what was meant by Chu and Zheng?

units.zh: 二人老耄，必傳言失旨，已相為斬之。
units.en: The two men were old and confused and must have transmitted words contrary to their intent, so I have beheaded them for you.
units.literal: The two men were old and confused and must have transmitted words contrary to their intent, so I have beheaded them for you.

units.zh: 若意有未已，可更遣年少有明決者來。」
units.en: If your intention is not yet exhausted, you may send another younger man with clarity and resolution."
units.literal: If your intention is not yet exhausted, you may send another younger man with clarity and resolution."

units.zh: 文懿復遣侍中衞演乞剋日送任。
units.en: Yuan tried again—Wei Yan begging a hostage deadline.
units.literal: Wenyi again sent attendant Wei Yan requesting a fixed day to deliver hostages.

units.zh: 帝謂演曰：「軍事大要有五，能戰當戰，不能戰當守，不能守當走，餘二事惟有降與死耳。
units.en: The emperor told Yan, "There are five essentials in military affairs: if one can fight, one should fight; if one cannot fight, one should defend; if one cannot defend, one should flee. The remaining two matters are only surrender and death.
units.literal: The emperor told Yan, "There are five essentials in military affairs: if one can fight, one should fight; if one cannot fight, one should defend; if one cannot defend, one should flee. The remaining two matters are only surrender and death.

units.zh: 汝不肯面縛，此為決就死也，不須送任。」
units.en: You are unwilling to bind yourself face-forward; this means you have decided to go to death. There is no need to send hostages."
units.literal: You are unwilling to bind yourself face-forward; this means you have decided to go to death. There is no need to send hostages."

units.zh: 文懿攻南圍突出，帝縱兵擊敗之，斬于梁水之上星墜之所。
units.en: Yuan rammed the southern sector; Sima Yi crushed him and struck off his head where the comet had plunged.
units.literal: Wenyi assaulted the southern siege line trying to break out; the Emperor unleashed troops, defeated him, and beheaded him at the spot where the star fell above the Liang River.

units.zh: 既入城，立兩標以別新舊焉。
units.en: Inside the walls twin posts marked who belonged to the revolt.
units.literal: After entering the city he erected two markers to separate new guilt from old inhabitants.

units.zh: 男子年十五已上七千餘人皆殺之，以為京觀。
units.en: Seven thousand males above fifteen died for the victory mound.
units.literal: All males fifteen sui and older—more than seven thousand—were executed to form a burial mound.

units.zh: 偽公卿已下皆伏誅，戮其將軍畢盛等二千餘人。
units.en: Phony ministers died with two thousand officers including Bi Sheng.
units.literal: All false dukes and ministers downward were executed; more than two thousand including general Bi Sheng were put to death.

units.zh: 收戶四萬，口三十餘萬。
units.en: Registers captured forty thousand households and three hundred thousand people.
units.literal: Households registered numbered forty thousand; mouths exceeded three hundred thousand.

units.zh: 初，文懿篡其叔父恭位而囚之。
units.en: Yuan had seized Uncle Gong’s seat and jailed him.
units.literal: Earlier Wenyi had usurped his uncle Gong’s position and imprisoned him.

units.zh: 及將反，將軍綸直、賈範等苦諫，文懿皆殺之。
units.en: On the eve of revolt Lun Zhi and Jia Fan pleaded—Yuan murdered them.
units.literal: When about to rebel generals Lun Zhi and Jia Fan remonstrated bitterly—Wenyi executed them all.

units.zh: 帝乃釋恭之囚，封直等之墓，顯其遺嗣。
units.en: Sima Yi freed Gong, rebuilt martyrs’ graves, and ennobled their sons.
units.literal: The Emperor then released Gong from prison, tended the tombs of Zhi and others, and honored their surviving heirs.

units.zh: 令曰：「古之伐國，誅其鯨鯢而已，諸為文懿所詿誤者，皆原之。
units.en: The order said, "In antiquity, when states were attacked, only their great criminals were executed. All those misled by Wenyì are pardoned.
units.literal: The order said, "In antiquity, when states were attacked, only their great criminals were executed. All those misled by Wenyì are pardoned.

units.zh: 中國人欲還舊鄉，恣聽之。」
units.en: If people from the Central States wish to return to their old villages, let them do so freely."
units.literal: If people from the Central States wish to return to their old villages, let them do so freely."

units.zh: 時有兵士寒凍，乞襦，帝弗之與。
units.en: Frozen troops begged quilts; he withheld them.
units.literal: At that time soldiers freezing in the cold begged for padded jackets; the Emperor did not grant them.

units.zh: 或曰：「幸多故襦，可以賜之。」
units.en: Someone said, "Fortunately there are many old padded jackets; they can be given to them."
units.literal: Someone said, "Fortunately there are many old padded jackets; they can be given to them."

units.zh: 帝曰：「襦者官物，人臣無私施也。」
units.en: The emperor said, "Padded jackets are government property; a minister may not dispense them privately."
units.literal: The emperor said, "Padded jackets are government property; a minister may not dispense them privately."

units.zh: 乃奏軍人年六十已上者罷遣千餘人，將吏從軍死亡者致喪還家。
units.en: He cashiered thousand greybeards and shipped coffins west.
units.literal: He then memorialized to discharge over a thousand soldiers aged sixty and above and to send home the remains of officers who died on campaign.

units.zh: 遂班師。
units.en: Then he marched home.
units.literal: Thereupon he withdrew the army.

units.zh: 天子遣使者勞軍于薊，增封食昆陽，并前二縣。
units.en: Envoys met him at Ji with fresh fiefs—Kunyang added to two older counties.
units.literal: The Son of Heaven dispatched envoys to reward the army at Ji, enlarged the grain income with Kunyang, together with the previous two counties.

units.zh: 初，帝至襄平，夢天子枕其膝，曰：「視吾面。」
units.en: Earlier, when the emperor reached Xiangping, he dreamed that the Son of Heaven rested his head on his knees and said, "Look at my face."
units.literal: Earlier, when the emperor reached Xiangping, he dreamed that the Son of Heaven rested his head on his knees and said, "Look at my face."

units.zh: 俛視有異於常，心惡之。
units.en: Stooping to look, it differed from the ordinary, and his heart abhorred it.
units.literal: Stooping to look it differed from the ordinary—his heart reviled it.

units.zh: 先是，詔帝便道鎮關中；
units.en: Orders already told him to guard Guanzhong by detour.
units.literal: Earlier an edict had ordered the Emperor by convenient route to hold Guanzhong;

units.zh: 及次白屋，有詔召帝，三日之間，詔書五至。
units.en: At Baiwu five summons arrived in three days.
units.literal: When halting at Baiwu edicts summoned the Emperor—within three days five edicts arrived.

units.zh: 手詔曰：「間側息望到，到便直排閤入，視吾面。」
units.en: The handwritten edict said, "I am lying on my side, breath held, hoping you arrive. When you arrive, push straight through the doors and enter; look at my face."
units.literal: The handwritten edict said, "I am lying on my side, breath held, hoping you arrive. When you arrive, push straight through the doors and enter; look at my face."

units.zh: 帝大遽，乃乘追鋒車晝夜兼行，自白屋四百餘里，一宿而至。
units.en: Panic drove the relay carriage four hundred li overnight.
units.literal: The Emperor was greatly alarmed and rode the pursuit-chariot day and night—more than four hundred li from Baiwu, arriving in one night.

units.zh: 引入嘉福殿臥內，升御牀。
units.en: He was led into the inner chamber of Jiafu Hall and helped onto the imperial couch.
units.literal: He was conducted into the Jiafu Palace inner chamber and helped onto the imperial couch.

units.zh: 帝流涕問疾，天子執帝手，目齊王曰：「以後事相託。
units.en: The emperor wept and asked about his illness. The Son of Heaven took the emperor's hand, looked at the Prince of Qi, and said, "I entrust later affairs to you.
units.literal: The emperor wept and asked about his illness. The Son of Heaven took the emperor's hand, looked at the Prince of Qi, and said, "I entrust later affairs to you.

units.zh: 死乃復可忍，吾忍死待君，得相見，無所復恨矣。」
units.en: Only now can I bear to die. I endured death waiting for you; having seen you, I have no further regret."
units.literal: Only now can I bear to die. I endured death waiting for you; having seen you, I have no further regret."

units.zh: 與大將軍曹爽並受遺詔輔少主。
units.en: He and Cao Shuang sealed regency for the boy emperor.
units.literal: Together with Grand General Cao Shuang he received testamentary edicts to aid the young lord.

units.zh: 及齊王即帝位，遷侍中、持節、都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事，與爽各統兵三千人，共執朝政，更直殿中，乘輿入殿。
units.en: When the Prince of Qi ascended the throne, Sima Yi was promoted to palace attendant, bearer of the staff of authority, commander-in-chief of all armies inside and outside the capital, and recorder of affairs of the Secretariat.
